title: A block-sign test needs 1.6 to 2.5 m/s for 90 percent recovery at 377 days in selected HD 1461 HIRES data
abstract: We measure sensitivity to a circular 377-day velocity wave in 215 selected HD 1461 HIRES nights. A phase-free two-coefficient score uses a 99 percent noise threshold from 9,999 residual block-sign draws. Separate draws test recovery over 72 phases and amplitudes from zero to 6 m/s. With season offsets and 30-day blocks, 90 percent recovery needs 1.60 to 2.45 m/s across the tested phases. Across the HIRES baseline and block checks, these limits span 1.60 to 2.45 m/s. The fitted 377-day amplitude is 0.49 m/s and its noise tail fraction is 0.74. The known 13.5-day signal passes the control test. HARPS gives better conditional sensitivity but can retain annual detector errors. This extends an earlier null transfer test with an amplitude-and-phase recovery map. The simulation assumes symmetric residual errors and independent time blocks. It does not fit physical stellar noise or give a planet exclusion limit. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and external retrieval steps are included. Source records stay outside the baseline bundle.
